name: People in history
hint: Invented people in a real age, where the great events break into their lives and force choices.

parts.title: The world as it was
chapters: Daily life
Show the age through an ordinary day in the main character's life, and what they want that the age makes hard.
The order
Who holds power, what is allowed and what it costs to break the rules. The reader learns them through a conflict.
The first sign
The historical events are heard from afar: a rumour, a letter, a rising price. Nobody yet knows what it means.

parts.title: History breaks in
chapters: What cannot be avoided
The real event reaches the characters' lives and shatters the everyday, so the main character has to choose.
The choice
The main character acts from the possibilities and mindset of their age, not those of a modern person.
New bonds, new enemies
The events put people on different sides. A relationship is made or broken by history.
The price
The choice has consequences by the age's own rules: shame, poverty, punishment or loss.

parts.title: In the thick of it
chapters: The great event
The historical moment seen through the main character's narrow view, not as a textbook overview.
The personal and the historical collide
What they want and what the age demands can no longer be reconciled.
All is lost
The lowest point. The course of history takes something that cannot be won back, and the main character cannot stop it.

parts.title: After the storm
chapters: The deciding choice
The historical outcome is fixed, but what the main character does with it is not. That is where the suspense lies.
The resolution
The invented people's fates are settled as the real events ebb away.
What remained
What the age left them with, and what the reader should understand about that time and their own.
The author's note
Written last: what is true, what you changed or invented, and why.
